title: AI-Driven Interface Design for Intelligent Tutoring System Improves Student Engagement
venue: Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether making the interface of an intelligent tutoring system (ITS) more AI-transparent and informative can increase student engagement. The authors argue that while ITS research often focuses on knowledge tracing and learning-path recommendation, less attention has been given to how interface design and explainable feedback affect whether students continue using the system.

The intervention is a set of AI-driven diagnostic-page designs in Santa, a mobile ITS for TOEIC preparation. Two interface versions are compared: page design A, which includes estimated score, part-by-part grades, a radar chart comparing users to peers, and a tutor-style comment; and page design B, which provides a more detailed and explainable breakdown of problem-solving analysis, skill proficiency, recommended lectures, similar-user progress, an adaptive curriculum, and an explanation window (“Santa Labs”) describing how AI outputs are computed. The system uses back-end models for score estimation, correctness, timeliness, dropout, and engagement prediction.

The study was conducted with new incoming users of Santa in South Korea, a large-scale online/mobile learning context for TOEIC, a standardized English test. The paper reports two controlled A/B tests: one comparing a diagnostic page with versus without the radar chart, and another comparing page designs A and B. Outcomes were engagement measures such as conversion rate, ARPU, total profit, and number of free questions consumed. Both experiments found that more AI-like, informative, and explainable interfaces improved engagement, with page B outperforming page A overall.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a controlled A/B test with large in-the-wild samples and random assignment, which gives it stronger causal credibility than correlational work. However, it is a product/company study with engagement outcomes only, and it lacks detailed statistical reporting such as confidence intervals or significance tests in the excerpt.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported gains are modest to moderate and consistently positive, with the largest effect around 25.13% on engagement-related metrics. The evidence suggests meaningful impact for a priority population using an ITS, but the outcomes are behavioral engagement rather than direct learning achievement.

interventions.use_case: mobile diagnostic and practice tutoring for TOEIC preparation with AI-generated score estimates, skill analytics, recommended lectures, adaptively offered curriculum, and explanatory UI components

finding.finding_summary: Controlled A/B tests in Santa showed that more explainable/AI-driven interface designs increased engagement outcomes. Adding a radar chart to page design A improved conversion rate, ARPU, total profit, and free-question consumption by up to 25.13% relative to the no-radar condition (n=2,877; 1,391 vs 1,486).
finding.measure: Conversion rate, Average Revenue Per User (ARPU), total profit, and average number of free questions consumed

finding.finding_summary: A second A/B test comparing page design B against page design A found that the more informative and explainable interface further improved engagement. Page design B increased conversion rate by 11.07%, ARPU by 10.29%, total profit by 12.57%, and free-question consumption by 7.19% (n=19,164; 9,442 vs 9,722).
finding.measure: Conversion rate, Average Revenue Per User (ARPU), total profit, and average number of free questions consumed
finding.effect_size: 11.07% to 12.57% gains on key engagement metrics
